title: Generalized birthday search: random k-XOR

problem.name: Generalized birthday search: random $k$-XOR
problem.statement_latex: Given $k$ lists $L_1,\ldots,L_k$ of uniformly random $n$-bit strings, find $x_i\in L_i$ with $x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_k=0$. The list lengths are part of the input. The single-solution regime uses lists of size about $2^{n/k}$; unrestricted-list variants permit larger lists. These problems model hash combiners, subset sums, and parts of decoding. Complexity is measured in classical list-processing time and quantum time or oracle queries, with coherent access to the prescribed random lists.
problem.statement_text: Given $k$ lists $L_1,\ldots,L_k$ of uniformly random $n$-bit strings, find $x_i\in L_i$ with $x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_k=0$. The list lengths are part of the input. quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(2^{n/(2+\lfloor\log_2k\rfloor)})$ time for unrestricted lists, quantum generalized birthday algorithms.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(2^{n/(2+\lfloor\log_2k\rfloor)})$ time for unrestricted lists, quantum generalized birthday algorithms.
quantum.details_latex: The list sizes in this setting can be chosen to support the merging strategy. For four prescribed random lists of size $2^{n/4}$, Schrottenloher gives $\widetilde O(2^{7n/24})$ quantum time in the single-solution regime. Its asymmetric merges, quantum search and quantum walks exploit that specific list-size promise. The fastest time bounds depend on the available memory and coherent lookup model; random-oracle $k$-XOR query lower bounds have scale $2^{n/(k+1)}$.

classical.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(2^{n/(1+\lfloor\log_2k\rfloor)})$ time with unrestricted lists, Wagner generalized birthday search.
classical.headline_text: $\widetilde O(2^{n/(1+\lfloor\log_2k\rfloor)})$ time with unrestricted lists, Wagner generalized birthday search.
classical.details_latex: Wagner uses lists of the corresponding size and successive prefix constraints. For four prescribed lists of size $2^{n/4}$, pair-list meet-in-the-middle costs $\widetilde O(2^{n/2})$ time. This is the comparator for the $7n/24$ quantum result. The unrestricted-list and prescribed-list problems have different input promises and are compared separately.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedups through smaller exponential constants in $n$ for fixed $k$. Amplitude amplification and quantum walks both appear in the merging constructions.
strength.description_text: Polynomial speedups through smaller exponential constants in $n$ for fixed $k$. Amplitude amplification and quantum walks both appear in the merging constructions.

evidence.description_latex: Partial evidence for time optimality, together with rigorous random-oracle query bounds. List size, number of solutions and memory model specify each comparison.

hardware.description_latex: The fastest methods require exponentially large lists with coherent access and fault-tolerant merging operations. Polynomial-qubit variants trade greater runtime for less coherent memory. Explicitly supplied lists also incur their stated loading and storage costs.
